_comment: Maximum age in days of the newest usable raster for a requested package
date. These are cadence-relative, not one flat number: a four-day
composite is structurally older than the day it covers.
v3 replaces the flat 3-day daily bound with the MEASURED domain-completion
lag from the latency store (modis_latency.py report --streams standard,
reports/latency/*_standard.jsonl, ~85 observed cadence dates ending
2026-08-13). Domain completion is when the LAST expected tile over the
national domain lands, which is what actually gates a usable date -- not
when the first granule appears. A combined MCD product completes when the
slower of its two platforms completes, so each bound below takes the max
over Terra and Aqua.
p50     p90     p95     max
MYD09GA       D+2.4   D+5.1   D+7.0   D+11.2   <- sets MCD09GA
MYD09CMG      D+2.4   D+5.3   D+6.9   D+10.1   <- sets MCD09CMG
The bounds are set from the observed MAX, rounded up, not the p95: a
breach is an operational alert and a package validation failure, so a p95
bound would fail roughly one day in twenty during normal operation. The
sample is ~3 months, so treat these as revisable once a longer store
exists -- widen them from measurement, never to silence an alert.
MCD15A3H (cadence 4): 12 = the D+8.7 completion max plus three days of
composite_fill, one anchor's worth. The 2002-2025 training anchor series
has 2125 four-day gaps, three eight-day, one twelve-day and one sixteen-
day, so 12 remains inside the staleness the model was trained on.
NDVIEVI is derived from scaled national MCD09GA and inherits its bound.
MCD12Q1 (annual): stale_by_design; publication lags the calendar year.
